courseDetails.title: SMART Goals Parenting
courseDetails.shortDescription: 5 Skills to Parenting Healthier and Easier. Bye-Bye Power Struggles!
courseDetails.longDescription:
Many parents describe the desires for their children as "I want my kids to be happy" or "I want them to have a good life." But these goals are abstract and difficult to achieve once, let alone repeat.


SMART Goals Parenting breaks these (and other) abstract desires down into their basic foundational components that allow you and your child to achieve happiness, connection, trust and respect... repeatedly.


SMART Goals Parenting's objective is to provide you with the knowledge and tools to cultivate your desired relationship with your child while also preparing your child for being able to one day cultivate happiness and success for him/herself.

You will learn the two SMART goals, which will be your guiding lights are you traverse the terrain of parenthood.


As long as you maintain your focus on what you are ultimately trying to achieve you won't get lost in the minutia.

After learning the SMART goals you will learn how to identify and avoid the pitfalls of choosing fear over love and discarding self-care.


Engaging in these two behaviors will sabotage all of your work. It will be like pouring water into a bottle with no bottom. If you have ever felt unappreciated, unloved, disrespected or criticized for your parenting efforts then I am certain one or both of these barriers are at play.

The next few lessons will tackle guidance.


My goal is to get you to the point when guiding your child is a simple conversation in which both of you feel understood and respected. Until then, you may need these skills to help you navigate.


Choices, Consequences, Rewards and Reinforce (CCRR) are the four parts of seamless discipline.


Streamline how you discipline and remove all power struggles. Doing so will solidify you as your child's respected figure and someone s/he can look up to.


The last, but not least topics covered are the most used parts of communication - listening and speaking. You should listen to understand and speak to build trust.


Many Parents, Myself included have practiced these, eliminating Parenting Stress, following Structured Guidance, helping to Raise Healthy, Confident and Motivated Children.


I look forward to helping you do the same.


Best regards,

Helen V Hicks MA MBA LPC

Licensed Professional Counselor, Parenting Coach
targetAudiences: Parents or caregivers of children aged 1 to 17 years old

Why advice does not work

A manager sees the answer and gives it. The employee nods, does it once and comes back with the same question. Advice solves today's task and leaves the person where they were. Coaching does the opposite: the person finds the answer, so they own it. This takes a structure for the conversation, good questions and the habit of listening, and none of that comes by itself.

What changes after this course

You open a conversation with a clear goal and a structure. You ask questions that make a person think and you can stay silent while they do. You give feedback that is heard. Your 1:1 meetings have an agenda and end with a step. You know when coaching fits and when the person needs a mentor, training or a direct instruction.

You can't tell if the memory loss is Alzheimer's or just aging. No lecture prepared you for the fear in their voice when they ask, "Am I losing my mind?" You want to help, but you don't know what "normal aging" even looks like.

These are not rare cases. They are every clinic, every hospital, every day.

Healthy aging is possible, but only when we stop pretending that tooth loss, falls, and memory decline are inevitable. Only when we stop confusing delirium with dementia. Only when we learn to prescribe safely for older bodies that metabolize drugs differently.

This course does not just teach geriatrics. It fills the gaps that leave patients afraid, clinicians uncertain, and students unprepared.

What You Will Learn

Have you ever wondered how your body detects and destroys invading microbes, prevents cancer, or remembers a past infection?

Immunology can seem like one of the most challenging subjects in medicine and life sciences. This course makes it easier through a structured, progressive learning approach. Instead of studying isolated facts, you will first develop a clear overview of the immune system, then explore its cells, organs, molecules, and mechanisms in greater detail, before connecting this knowledge to real biological and clinical situations.

You will discover how the innate and adaptive immune systems cooperate to protect the body, how antigens are recognized, and how antibodies, cytokines, complement proteins, and immune cells coordinate immune responses. You will also explore inflammation, antigen presentation, MHC molecules, immune regulation, and the mechanisms that maintain immune balance.

Building on these foundations, the course examines what happens when immune mechanisms become defective or overactive. You will explore important topics such as immunodeficiency, hypersensitivity, allergies, autoimmune diseases, transplantation immunology, and immune-mediated disorders.

Finally, you will connect fundamental immunological principles to important medical and laboratory applications, including vaccination, tumor immunology, cancer immunotherapy, monoclonal antibodies, and immunodiagnostics.

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

  • Identify the major organs, tissues, and cells of the immune system.

  • Explain antigen presentation and the roles of MHC class I and class II molecules.

  • Understand the complement system, cytokines, inflammation, and immune regulation.

  • Describe the mechanisms of cellular and antibody-mediated immune responses.

  • Understand the immunological basis of hypersensitivity, allergy, autoimmunity, and immunodeficiency.

  • Relate immune mechanisms to transplantation and tumor immunology.

  • Understand the principles behind vaccination, immunotherapy, monoclonal antibodies, and immunological diagnostic techniques.

  • Connect fundamental immunological concepts to relevant clinical and laboratory applications.

Whether you are studying immunology for the first time or reviewing important concepts for professional development, this course will help you build a stronger conceptual foundation and understand how the immune system protects the body — and what happens when its balance is disrupted.

Welcome to Poultry Viral Diseases: The Essential Field Guide for Veterinarians and Farm Managers.

I'm Mohamed Alashram, and in this course, we will explore one of the most important challenges in modern poultry production: recognizing, diagnosing, and controlling viral diseases before they cause devastating losses.

Imagine visiting a poultry farm where birds have started coughing, feed consumption is declining, and egg production is falling. The vaccination program appears to be complete, and the farm's management seems satisfactory. Yet something is wrong.

Is it Newcastle disease? Infectious bronchitis? Avian influenza? Or could another infection, a management problem, or a combination of factors explain the findings?

The answer cannot be based on a single clinical sign or a photograph of a lesion. It requires a systematic investigation.

Throughout this course, we will develop that investigative approach step by step.

We will study major poultry viral diseases, including Newcastle disease, avian influenza, infectious bronchitis, infectious bursal disease, Marek's disease, infectious laryngotracheitis, avian reovirus infections, chicken infectious anemia, fowlpox, and avian encephalomyelitis.

For each disease, we will connect the underlying virology with what you actually encounter in the field: clinical signs, flock performance records, post-mortem findings, laboratory tests, vaccination history, and practical control decisions.

You will learn how to conduct a structured flock investigation, perform a basic poultry necropsy, select appropriate diagnostic samples, understand the roles of PCR and ELISA, and interpret laboratory results in the context of the clinical picture.

We will also examine why vaccination programs sometimes fail, how immunosuppressive diseases compromise flock health, and how effective biosecurity can reduce the risk of introducing and spreading viral pathogens.

Most importantly, we will use practical cases to develop your diagnostic reasoning. You will be encouraged to ask the right questions, compare differential diagnoses, identify missing evidence, and decide what action should follow.

Remember one fundamental principle: recognizing a disease is not the same as confirming it. Good poultry health management combines clinical observation, sound epidemiological investigation, appropriate laboratory testing, and timely veterinary action.

For suspected highly pathogenic avian influenza or virulent Newcastle disease, rapid notification and appropriate official control measures are essential.

Whether you are a poultry veterinarian, farm manager, production supervisor, consultant, or veterinary student, this course is designed to help you approach viral disease problems with greater confidence, scientific discipline, and practical understanding.

Let's begin by examining why poultry viral diseases remain such a major challenge for flock health, farm profitability, and the sustainability of the poultry industry.
